plan.name: New features: manual product entry, containers, icon picker, product list UX, wide layout, mixed-photo classification
plan.conventions: This plan implements the specs proposed in PR #397 (docs/specs/39-batch-containers.md, 40-icon-picker.md, 41-mixed-photo-classification.md, and amendments to 05-frontend-pwa-foundations.md, 16-product-maintenance.md, 02-data-model.md, 06-vision-shelf-ingestion.md, 07-shopping-list-reconciliation.md, 09-consumption-logging.md). If PR #397 has not merged into main by the time a package starts, read the relevant spec file from its branch directly - git show origin/specs/new-features-proposal:docs/specs/<file> - never guess at the contract, and never implement from anything but the spec text itself. Every package that changes products.js touches a shared file three other packages in this same wave also touch (the list, the batch list, and the edit form are different regions of the same file, which is why this wave runs sequentially rather than in parallel) - read what the previous package in the wave actually shipped before touching the same file, and do not reformat or reorder a region another package owns. Apply the silent invariants from CLAUDE.md throughout: 404-not-403 for unknown AND inaccessible storages and for the whole admin area, with an identical response either way; is_admin re-queried from the DB on every admin request, never returned in any JSON and never a client-side branch; debug_reason only when APP_ENV is dev, emitted from the single error serializer; same-storage validation on every id - path, parent_id, move target, confirm-body field, and (new in this plan) container id references, which are enforced structurally per 39 rather than by a runtime check - read that spec's own reasoning before assuming a check is missing; every inventory_batches write paired, in the same transaction, with an inventory_logs row - note that 39's container operations (label set/clear, destroy) write NO inventory_logs row, since no quantity changes, which is deliberate and spec'd, not an omission; EXIF stripped from every upload with orientation applied to pixels FIRST; expiry cascades touching derived dates only, never user ones. Every build, test and migration runs through docker compose - no host toolchain, per docs/specs/01-architecture-and-deployment.md. Any package that adds or renames a file under web/static/ belonging to the cached app shell (icon-picker.js is one) adds it to SHELL_ASSETS in web/static/sw.js and bumps CACHE_VERSION. Every new user-visible string goes through spec 19's catalogs, with the key in both en.json and de.json. e2e/fixtures/seed.sql: add rows to the shared E2E Household storage following that file's own established pattern (one product/batch per scenario, next free id range, ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING) rather than one storage per package; never write durable per-user state (start_page, barcode_prompt_seen_at) onto a shared fixture user.

packages.spec: Issue 398: wide layout becomes the default for every page
packages.focus: Implement spec 05's Layout width amendment exactly: flip every page's <header> and <main> from class="shell" to class="shell--wide" - index.html, storages.html, locations.html, categories.html, products.html, ingest.html, shopping-list.html, review.html, consume-review.html, dashboard.html. inventory.html already uses shell--wide (spec 33) and needs no change. Leave .shell itself defined in css/base.css untouched as a class - a component that wants a narrow column within an otherwise-wide page may still use it locally; only the per-page header/main default moves. No JS changes, no behavior changes beyond the visual width - this is the smallest possible package on purpose, since three later packages in this same wave build on top of products.html and should not also have to resolve a layout-class merge conflict. Verify visually (or via an E2E boundingBox/computed-width assertion) that each page's main element is now capped at 80rem, not 40rem. Do not touch the responsive stacked-card breakpoint behavior spec 33 already defines for inventory.html's table - that is unrelated to this package and belongs to whichever later package in this wave adds a second table (W2).

packages.spec: Issue 399: product list default-to-filter, standalone add-product entry point
packages.focus: Implement spec 16's two new sections, The product list and Creating a product, together since both reshape the same page. Backend: POST /api/storages/{storage_id}/products, body {name, category_id?, item_type?, min_stock?, image?, icon_name?} - only name required (422 otherwise, mirroring internal/httpapi/shoppinglists.go's existing manual-entry validation), runs the matching service's stage 1 against name before inserting and returns the existing product on a close hit instead of creating a duplicate, creates no initial batch. Frontend, web/static/js/pages/products.js: replace the always-rendered btn btn--block btn--ghost button list with a filter-only default (nothing rendered until a search query or a new Show all products button), and once shown, render results as a table reusing inventory.html's row markup and CSS classes directly (read web/static/js/pages/inventory.js's renderBatchRow/productCell and the .inventory-table__* CSS first - extract whatever needs extracting into a shared module rather than copy-pasting the table markup into products.js, since spec 16 is explicit this must not become a second table implementation). Add a + Add product button opening the manual-entry form (name, category, item type, min_stock, optional picture via the existing js/image-picker.js) - reuse the same field set and image-picker call web/static/js/pages/shopping-list.js's describeManually() already uses rather than building a second form from scratch. Clearing the search box returns to the filter-only empty state, never back to show-all. This package runs after W1 (wide layout) - build on integration/newfeatures-welle-1 once that package has merged into it, not from an earlier state of products.html.

Implement spec 39 in full - this is the largest and most novel package in this wave, hence opus/xhigh. Migration: containers table and inventory_batches.container_id exactly as spec 02's amended schema section shows (read it, not just 39, for the exact column list and index). Backend: container_label/container_type as upsert-or-rename fields on the existing PATCH /api/storages/{storage_id}/inventory-batches/{id} (creating a container on first set, renaming the same row on a later set, clearing without destroying on null); POST /api/storages/{storage_id}/containers/{id}/destroy (sets destroyed_at, clears container_id on every batch referencing it, in one transaction, 404 on unknown or already-destroyed - destroying is not idempotent); container_disposition (source default/target/both/neither/destroy) as a new optional field on the existing split endpoint, per the exact table in spec 39's Splitting section - a no-op on a container-less source batch regardless of value, and destroy running in the same transaction as the split itself, never a two-step client-visible window. No inventory_logs row for any container operation - nothing about quantity changed; this is deliberate, confirm you have not added one. Frontend, products.js's batch list (the same page W2 rewrote - read what W2 actually shipped for the batch-list region before touching it): a container label/type field per batch with inline rename/clear and a destroy action (with confirmation, since destroy clears every batch referencing it, not just the one in view); a container_disposition radio group on the split form, shown only when the source batch has a container, defaulting to source. E2E: cover labeling, renaming, each container_disposition value on a split, and destroy - the 22-in-the-pack, 2-in-the-fridge-with-no-container shape spec 39 exists for is the core scenario to prove.

packages.spec: Issue 401: icon picker with alias search
packages.focus: Implement spec 40 in full. Migration: the global icon_aliases table exactly as spec 40's schema section shows, including the trigram index (pg_trgm is already enabled per spec 02). Backend: GET /api/storages/{storage_id}/icon-suggestions?query= - query icon_aliases first (trigram-similar, ordered by similarity), then Iconify's own /search via the existing Iconify.Candidates client (internal/imagesearch/providers.go) reused rather than a second HTTP integration, merge local hits first deduplicated by icon_name then Iconify hits not already present, cap at the same limit=10 Iconify.Candidates already uses; local results must still return if Iconify is unreachable, per the fail-soft posture spec 07 already established for the picture flow. POST /api/storages/{storage_id}/icon-suggestions/aliases {icon_name, alias} - insert ON CONFLICT (icon_name, alias) DO NOTHING, any authenticated storage member may call it, not admin-gated. Frontend: new web/static/js/icon-picker.js, sibling to js/image-picker.js and following its established shape (search input, clickable result grid rendering actual icons not text, loading/empty/provider-down states) - replaces the free-text icon_name <input> on products.html's edit form (the same page W2/W3 also touched - read what they shipped for that region first). Picking an Iconify-only result must silently call the alias-recording endpoint with the exact search term typed, no confirmation step. Add icon-picker.js to SHELL_ASSETS in web/static/sw.js and bump CACHE_VERSION. E2E: search, pick an Iconify-only result, search the same term again and confirm it now returns as a local hit, clear an icon.

packages.spec: Issue 402: mixed-photo shopping-list classification, finishing the photo shopping-list stub
packages.focus: Implement spec 41 in full, including finishing spec 07's already-specified but never-built photo shopping-list path (currently 501 not_implemented in internal/httpapi/shoppinglists.go - read 07's Ingestion section, it already describes the correct target behavior, this package just has to build it). First, 07's stub: POST /api/storages/{storage_id}/shopping-lists with source: photo - multipart upload, background job, Gemini extracts shopping_list_lines, each line through the existing matching service exactly as a text-source list already uses (internal/matching, shared with 06). Second, spec 41's classification: add looks_like_shopping_list (bool) and shopping_list_lines (string array) to the Gemini response schema and prompts for ModeShelf, ModeProduct and ModeConsumption (internal/vision/gemini.go's Mode type and prompts map is the extension point - one call, no added latency on the common case where the field comes back false). Third, the from_job_id variant of the same shopping-lists endpoint: given an existing shelf_ingestion/product_photo/consumption job whose stored analysis has looks_like_shopping_list true and non-empty lines, create the shopping list directly from those lines with no second upload and no second Gemini call, mark the origin job discarded (06's existing job-status vocabulary), 404 on a job that does not qualify or has already been reclassified once. Frontend: a banner on that job's normal review screen (web/static/js/review.js and/or the mode-specific review pages, 06/09) naming the mode the photo was captured under, with two actions - Process as shopping list (calls from_job_id, navigates to the new list's resolution screen) and Keep as [original kind] (dismisses the banner, proceeds through the job's ordinary review unchanged, including when items came back empty). Do not touch 09's sticky capture-mode selector itself - it is explicitly unchanged by this spec, read the What this deliberately does not do section before assuming otherwise. This package is file-disjoint from W1-W4 (internal/vision, internal/httpapi/shoppinglists.go, review.js - not products.html/products.js) but still runs last in this sequential wave; nothing in it actually depends on the other four having landed. E2E: stub a shelf-photo analysis response carrying looks_like_shopping_list true, assert the banner appears, cover both actions including that keep-as-shelf leaves the (empty) item review intact and process-as-shopping-list lands on a real resolvable list.
